Run the model

Source: R/run_model.R
run_model.Rd

Runs every priority ordering of every scenario of the model. With the default priorities = "all" and k satellite accounts, there are k! orderings per scenario, with ECO last. The number of sectors and of accounts comes from the database.

Usage

run_model(
  io,
  model = NULL,
  scenarios = NULL,
  orderings = NULL,
  strict = FALSE,
  verbose = interactive(),
  lock_tolerance = NULL
)

Arguments

io

Path of a model.yml, or a lexio_io object.

model

A lexio_model object (when io is the database).

scenarios

Scenarios to run (names; default: all).

orderings

Orderings to run (numbers or labels; default: all of the model).

strict

If TRUE, stops at the first non-optimal level. With FALSE (default), runs everything and records the status of each level, shown in the summary and in the report.

verbose

Show progress.

lock_tolerance

Replaces the lock_tolerance of the model (see define_model()); NULL (default) uses the one of the model.

Value

Object of class lexio_results: the model, the database, the runs (runs, one per scenario x ordering), the summary (summarize_runs()) and metadata. Use write_outputs() to write everything to a folder.

Details

The simplest call passes the path of a model.yml: the model says where the database is (data). The database and the model can also be passed as objects (declare_io(), define_model()).

Examples

res <- run_model(system.file("examples", "toy", "model.yml", package = "lexio"), verbose = FALSE)
res
#> <lexio_results> toy | 3 sectors | 3 account(s): E, I, LAB | corridor: two-sided corridor 
#>   scenario E_shock        6 ordering(s) | all optimal | 3 distinct state(s)
#>   scenario I_shock        6 ordering(s) | all optimal | 1 distinct state(s)
#>   distinct states in total: 4 
#>   write everything with write_outputs(res, "folder")
head(res$summary$runs)
